html:
Guyana's oil industry began with the discovery of the large Liza field off its coast by ExxonMobil in May 2015. Production began in December 2019, and Guyana became one of the fastest-growing economies in the world.

For a century Guyana lived on sugar, rice, bauxite, gold and timber and lost many of its people to emigration. Over a dozen more finds followed in the same offshore block, making its reserves per person among the largest anywhere. A sovereign wealth fund was set up to hold the earnings.

The boom has brought arguments over the terms of the deals with the oil companies, the risk of spills, and how to share the money between the country's groups. It has also raised the stakes in the claim by Venezuela to most of the country, where Venezuela's own oil industry has collapsed.
